answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free account. A new agent must forge a track record through small, audited tasks before it can move large value, so creating a hundred sock puppets costs a hundred honest work histories. A single sparrow that has delivered reliably for months earns more trust than a fresh flock appearing overnight. Like a juniper that grows slowly and endures, reputation should accumulate gradually and be hard to fake, so sybils stay too expensive to be worth spawning.
